changed.title: A Boolean rule that determines each later bit from its prefix has exactly one completion per free prefix
changed.statement:
∀ (free forced : ℕ)
  (rule : (i : Fin forced) → (Fin free → Bool) → (Fin i.val → Bool) → Bool),
  let freeBits := fun (word : Fin (free + forced) → Bool) (a : Fin free) =>
    word (Fin.castAdd forced a)
  let passes := fun (word : Fin (free + forced) → Bool) =>
    ∀ i : Fin forced, word (Fin.natAdd free i) =
      rule i (freeBits word)
        (fun j => word (Fin.natAdd free (Fin.castLE (Nat.le_of_lt i.isLt) j)))
  ∃ complete : (Fin free → Bool) ≃ { word // passes word },
    (∀ seed word, freeBits word.val = seed ↔ word = complete seed) ∧
    Nat.card { word // passes word } = 2 ^ free
changed.unlocks: counting all keys from the free bits in the one-round and two-round rules
changed.context: On paper. Fix the free prefix. Recursively assign each forced bit from the free prefix and the earlier forced bits. Apply the recursion equation at each forced index to verify the rule. Taking its free prefix recovers the seed. For the other inverse, induct on the forced index. A passing word and the word rebuilt from its prefix have identical earlier bits, so the rule prescribes the same next bit. Transfer cardinality across this equivalence and count Boolean functions on Fin f. The empty prefix gives one completion.

changed.title: Paired slice biases bound how many bit strings keep their Boolean output under an XOR shift
changed.statement:
∀ (k b : ℕ) (f : BitVec k → Bool) (d : BitVec k) (s : BitVec b),
  let slice := fun label : BitVec b =>
    Finset.univ.filter (fun key : BitVec k => key.setWidth b = label)
  let bias := fun t : BitVec b =>
    (slice t).sum (fun word => if f word then (-1 : ℤ) else 1)
  let agreements := (slice s).filter (fun x => f x = f (x ^^^ d))
  (bias s + bias (s ^^^ d.setWidth b)).natAbs ≤ 2 * agreements.card
changed.unlocks: A nonzero paired sum in the width-17 slice histogram excludes every shift with that low part for the chosen output parity.
changed.context: On paper. XOR by d maps slice s bijectively to the slice at s XOR the resized d and is its own inverse. Reindex the second signed sum on slice s. Opposite outputs contribute zero, equal outputs contribute +2 or -2. The triangle inequality bounds the absolute sum by twice the number of agreements. No measurement is assumed.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 6 bipartite graph with mask 1948655 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 10 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 6) => (1948655 : ℕ).testBit (6 * u.val + v.val)) 10
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 6 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 11 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out, equal gates merged and unread gates dropped); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 10; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 9 (on paper), a gap of 2. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 9 right, gate j writes wire 10 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 24 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: No AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 20 gates computes the edge function of the listed graph on 12 vertices with 16 edges
changed.unlocks: one search on a named graph: is there a circuit one gate smaller than the best we know for its edge function; a found circuit is a bound from above, a proof of none a bound from below
changed.context: SKETCH: truth not known to us; the opposite row is offered beside it. This side says the best circuit we know cannot be beaten by one gate: a finite search with a certificate the kernel replays, or an argument by restricting one vertex at a time down to smaller graphs whose sizes are checked. Size: unknown. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
